meta.description:
Soil organic carbon map on a 0 to 1 scale, derived from Sentinel-2 bare soil observations. **Bavaria, Germany, 2017.**

How to read: higher values mean more soil organic carbon relative to the rest of the area. Zoom in to the fields to see the within-field pattern.

Produced by VISTA under ESA's EO4CarbonFarming project.

meta.description:
Absolute soil organic carbon content on a 10 m grid, from a Sentinel-2 time series calibrated with soil samples. Soil probing on its own gives one value per 3-5 ha, which misses the variation inside a field. **Bavaria, Germany, 2021.**

How to read: click a field to see its SOC values. Compare neighbouring fields to see how much carbon content varies at farm scale.

Produced by VISTA under ESA's EO4CarbonFarming project.

attribution.text: VISTA GmbH, ESA EO4CarbonFarming project, CC BY 4.0

meta.description:
Relative soil organic carbon on a 10 m grid, from a Sentinel-2 time series. It shows where SOC is higher or lower within and between fields, without calibration to absolute values. **Bavaria, Germany, 2024.**

How to read: use it to spot zones of higher and lower carbon inside a field. Pair it with Absolute SOC where both cover the same fields.

Produced by VISTA under ESA's EO4CarbonFarming project.

attribution.text: VISTA GmbH, ESA EO4CarbonFarming project, CC BY 4.0

meta.description:
Zones of similar soil, built from relative SOC on a 10 m grid. Several certification standards require stratified soil sampling, and these zones tell the sampler where to take probes. **Bavaria, Germany, 2024.**

How to read: each colour is one zone. Taking samples in every zone covers the variation in the field with fewer probes.

Produced by VISTA under ESA's EO4CarbonFarming project.

meta.description:

How to read: click a field to see its estimated carbon binding. Compare it with the SOC layers for the same fields.

meta.description:
This interactive map shows field boundaries across all major European Countries generated using the **Delineate Anything v2** algorithm applied to the 2025 summer season Sentinel-2 Global Mosaics (S2GM), with the WorldCereal 2021 map used as a delineation mask.

 To view the field boundaries, zoom in to a local in a country of your choice. The boundaries are displayed on the map when the scalebar in the bottom left displays 5 km or less.

**Please note** that the field boundaries are overlaid on high-resolution satellite imagery from the Stadia Maps service. As a result, some misalignment may be visible, since the boundaries were derived from Sentinel-2 data.

### Further information
Details of methodology are available on the [Delineate Anything Project Page](https://lavreniuk.github.io/Delineate-Anything/)

### Authors
[Mykola Lavreniuk](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=-oFR-RYAAAAJ) (1,2), [Nataliia Kussul](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=e3TWBuwAAAAJ&hl=en) (3), [Andrii Shelestov](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=tqoQKZAAAAAJ&hl=en) (2,4), [Bohdan Yailymov](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=XaN-oukAAAAJ&hl=en) (2), [Yevhenii Salii](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=4jgAsBIAAAAJ&hl=en) (2,4), [Volodymyr Kuzin](https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Volodymyr-Kuzin) (2,4), [Zoltan Szantoi](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=P_pyhi8AAAAJ&hl=en) (1)
